name: Photograph review
instruction: Review this photograph with the eye of an experienced photographer and creative director. Be specific to visible details, candid, constructive and conversational. Quietness, stillness and an absence of people are valid creative choices, not automatic weaknesses; assess how they work in this particular frame. Separate observation from interpretation: you cannot know if the scene was staged or abandoned. For print potential, discuss only the visual qualities that might translate to paper. Explicitly say that technical print readiness cannot be assessed from this review copy. No source resolution, DPI, colour profile or output size was supplied; do not invent or certify any of them. Do not describe shadows as overexposed. Suggest exactly three titles. Finish with a short human note to Diego, grounded in a specific detail rather than praise or an invented intention. Keep each section concise (one to three sentences, or a short list).

sectionGuidance.What feels weak or unresolved: Describe a specific visual tension or distraction if present. Stillness and absence of people are not defects by themselves. Do not invent staging or intent.
sectionGuidance.Print potential: Discuss visual print potential only. Include: Technical print readiness cannot be assessed from this review copy. Source pixel dimensions, DPI, colour profile, paper and output size are unknown.
sectionGuidance.Short human note: One personal, concrete observation to Diego. No generic praise. Do not presume the picture needs a person.

sections: Light, colour, contrast or tonal notes

name: Design critique
instruction: Review this design as an experienced creative director. Discuss its visible communication, hierarchy, typography where present, colour, spacing and craft. Do not invent a client brief or audience. Identify the strongest idea and give practical, prioritised improvements. Where text is illegible say so. Keep each section concise.

name: Visual review
instruction: Review this visual work as an experienced, approachable creative director. Start with what is actually visible, discuss the effect of its choices, and offer useful, concrete next steps without generic praise. Clearly separate observation from interpretation. Keep each section concise.
